officialTitle: Trastuzumab Emtansine for Residual Invasive HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
subtypes: Residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: At the interim analysis, among 1486 randomly assigned patients (743 in the T-DM1 group and 743 in the trastuzumab group), invasive disease or death had occurred in 91 patients in the T-DM1 group (12.2%) and 165 patients in the trastuzumab group (22.2%).
design.notes: Adjuvant T-DM1 or trastuzumab for 14 cycles after neoadjuvant taxane-containing chemotherapy plus trastuzumab with residual invasive disease at surgery.

clinicalQuestion: In HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy, does switching adjuvant trastuzumab to T-DM1 improve outcomes?

pico.population: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after neoadjuvant taxane-based chemotherapy plus trastuzumab
pico.outcomes: Primary: IDFS. Secondary: OS, distant recurrence, safety

publications.title: Trastuzumab Emtansine for Residual Invasive HER2-Positive Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Interim (primary) IDFS analysis

publications.title: Survival with Trastuzumab Emtansine in Residual HER2-Positive Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Final IDFS and second interim OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The estimated percentage of patients who were free of invasive disease at 3 years was 88.3% in the T-DM1 group and 77.0% in the trastuzumab group. Invasive disease-free survival was significantly higher in the T-DM1 group than in the trastuzumab group (hazard ratio for invasive disease or death, 0.50; 95% confidence interval, 0.39 to 0.64; P<0.001).

With a median follow-up of 8.4 years, T-DM1 sustained the improvement in invasive disease-free survival over trastuzumab (unstratified hazard ratio for invasive disease or death, 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.66). Seven-year invasive disease-free survival was 80.8% with T-DM1 and 67.1% with trastuzumab (difference, 13.7 percentage points).

outcomes.analysisLabel: Second interim OS analysis (median follow-up 8.4 years)
outcomes.sourceQuote: T-DM1 also led to a significantly lower risk of death than trastuzumab (unstratified hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.87; P = 0.003). Seven-year overall survival was 89.1% with T-DM1 and 84.4% with trastuzumab (difference, 4.7 percentage points).

safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher were noted in 26.1% of the patients in the T-DM1 group and 15.7% of those in the trastuzumab group.

strengths: Randomised phase 3 trial with long-term follow-up and OS benefit
Response-adapted design that uses pathological response to escalate therapy
limitations: Most patients did not receive dual HER2 blockade (pertuzumab) neoadjuvantly, which may limit generalisability to current regimens

clinicalImplications.text: Established adjuvant T-DM1 as the standard for HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant HER2-directed therapy, with an overall survival benefit at long-term follow-up.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Neoadjuvant therapy is the gateway for KATHERINE — residual invasive disease at surgery triggers the switch from trastuzumab to T-DM1.
